correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, the first-run equations g±=a±(p±+q±g∓) with a±=lambda/(lambda∓ikc) give a denominator proportional to lambda²d+c²k² and the averaged numerator lambda²d+ikc lambda delta. The transforms of the normalized positive half-line densities match; their identical conditional magnitude densities prove sign independence and exclude an atom. The inverse follows from d=2m−m²+delta²: the lower bound m>|delta| is equivalent to d>2|delta| and the upper bound m+|delta|<1 to d<1 on the admissible branch. At d=1 the inverse tends to probabilities 1 and 1−2|delta|; on the oblique edges it tends to d and 0, and at the vertex to 0 and 0. These limits establish all boundary assertions of the revised text. Independent Poisson parity summation uses survival weights r^(2j) and r^(2j)(q++q−)/2 for even and odd counts respectively. Differentiation using H″=H gives h′=(lambda r)²(A²−1)/H², with r²(A²−1)=delta². This proves the endpoints, strictness, and equality case under the stated assumptions.
residual_risks: The supplied finite numerical and Monte Carlo checks are corroboration, not the basis of correctness; no formal verification claimed. The boundary is a closure of parameter pairs, not a statement that all boundary models have finite T.

value.rationale: The sharp inverse region is useful when only an exact terminal marginal is available: it both tests compatibility with the proposed asymmetric mechanism and uniquely identifies its directional probabilities at known speed and event rate. The exponential magnitude alone loses direction information, whereas the sign restores it; the lifetime's nonconstant hazard independently distinguishes asymmetric killing. The corrected boundary describes the degeneracies, not merely an example computed from a standard resolvent.
residual_risks: Identifiability is conditional on known speed/event rate and the precisely specified observation/model assumptions, not a finite-sample inference guarantee.
